sends.connect: a TCP connect; the connection is closed after the read
sends.greeting: nothing: the scanner only reads what the service sends first
sends.http: one HTTP request for the root page (method GET, path "/") with User-Agent "CyberView-Scanner/1.0.0 (authorized vulnerability scan, detection only; +https://xanderhutch.github.io/CyberView/vulnerabilities.html#scanner)"
sends.tls: a standard TLS handshake (the certificate is read, never trusted or used)
sends.paths: only with --paths (off by default): at most 8 extra HTTP GET requests per host, each for a frozen literal path in scanner/lib/paths.mjs and only when that host's own root page, headers, certificate or port already hint at the product; same User-Agent, redirects recorded, not followed, only a product/version token kept

profile.name: custom ports
limits: Only the 4 listed TCP port(s) were checked; a service on any other port was not seen.
UDP was not checked (run with --udp for the DNS, NTP and SNMP checks).
Web: one GET / per web port; no other path was requested, so an application under another path was not seen.
TLS: one handshake per TLS port; a different client may negotiate different parameters.
A host that answered on none of the listed ports is reported as unreachable, not as clean.

notes: Detection only: versions were read from what each service states about itself. A service can hide or misstate its version, and a Linux distribution's package can carry a backported fix under an old version number; confidence says which.

Matching uses CyberView's known-exploited flaws (CISA's KEV catalog with NVD's affected-version ranges) and recent high-risk flaws; a flaw outside them is not reported. A clean result is not proof that a host has no vulnerabilities.

The CyberView rating is the CVSS base score adjusted for exploitation evidence (CVSS v3.1 Exploit Code Maturity), the same calculation as the Vulnerabilities page; every point is listed with each finding.
Exploitation analyses and fix guides on the linked pages are written by CyberView AI (a Claude model) from vendor and government sources.
1 matched CVE(s) had no CVE lookup row in the data used; their rating is computed from the KEV entry alone (marked in each finding).
